Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Vitalis MedTech Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Mark Ellison, CEO; Rachel Kim, CFO; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Ellison.

Mark Ellison:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Vitalis MedTech delivered solid results this quarter, driven by strong execution and continued demand for our innovative medical device solutions.

Today, I will cover four key aspects of our performance: procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary; competitive dynamics and market share trends; key assumptions underlying our guidance; and organic revenue growth by segment and geography.

Rachel will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary.

In the MedTech industry, procedure volumes form the foundation of our business model, directly influencing the use of our capital equipment such as the VeriFlex robotic navigation systems, along with consumables like PrecisionGuide catheters and OrthoForge implants. We're happy to share that we experienced strong growth in procedures across our primary areas during the third quarter, signaling a market recovery that's now solidly in expansion mode following the COVID disruptions.

On the top-line figures, we observed a 14% year-over-year increase in global procedure volumes, picking up from 11% in the second quarter and representing our most robust growth since 2019 pre-pandemic benchmarks. Sequentially, volumes increased by 5%, propelled by the resolution of seasonal backlogs in orthopedics and cardiovascular segments. This performance exceeded the industry average of around 10% year-over-year growth, based on our benchmarking against competitors like Stryker and Intuitive Surgical, resulting in roughly 120 basis points of market share expansion in our focus areas.

Diving into the franchises:

In cardiovascular, which accounts for 45% of our revenue, volumes rose 16% year-over-year, powered by increased structural heart and electrophysiology interventions. Our Watchman Flex occlusion devices achieved 22% growth in procedures, aided by expanded labeling allowing TEE-optional use and compelling real-world data from the PINNACLE FLX registry, highlighting a 75% reduction in stroke risk compared to warfarin. Ablation procedures using our RhythmSync RF platform climbed 19%, as we took share from Boston Scientific's Farapulse PFA system due to their ongoing supply issues. TAVR cases, in a maturing market, advanced 8% with the EvoCore valve, backed by data akin to PARTNER 3 trials showing excellent hemodynamics.

Orthopedics, comprising 30% of revenue, posted 12% year-over-year volume growth, with hip and knee replacements surging 15% from pent-up demand. The Triad Cementless Acetabular System led with 25% growth in primary hip cases, attributable to its hydroxyapatite coating technology that cuts aseptic loosening rates to below 1% at five years. Spine fusions increased 9%, though we noted some weakness in supporting technologies like NeuroStim neuromodulation leads owing to surgeon staffing constraints—operating room utilization stood at 82% against our 90% goal.

In neuromodulation and other areas, making up 25% of revenue, volumes grew 13% year-over-year, spearheaded by 18% expansion in deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's using our NeuroVive directional leads, which deliver 30% superior symptom control according to ADVANCE trial results. Chronic pain spinal cord stimulation procedures rose 11%, but pricing remained steady amid pressure from Nevro's HF10 waveform.

Geographically, the recovery shows variation but positive momentum:

The U.S., representing 60% of volumes, surged 17% year-over-year, now 5% above 2019 levels. Elective backlogs have mostly cleared, supported by CMS reimbursement increases for MS-DRGs—such as 4.5% for TAVR under DRG 273—and better hospital staffing, with nurse-to-bed ratios improving 15% per AHA figures, freeing up OR slots. We're also benefiting from obesity-related trends, boosting bariatric-linked ortho volumes by 20%.

Europe, at 25%, grew 9% year-over-year, trailing due to NHS waitlists topping 7.6 million procedures and German DRG adjustments lowering average selling prices by 3%. That said, our Q2 CE Mark for the next-generation VeriFlex robot has sped adoption in France and Benelux, expanding the installed base 25% and pushing utilization to 75%.

Asia-Pacific, 15% of volumes, bounced back to 12% year-over-year growth, with China at 20% after easing zero-COVID policies. Our collaboration with Mindray on localized OrthoForge kits yielded 30% procedural share gains in joint replacements, accessing a $15 billion total addressable market expanding at 9% CAGR driven by aging populations.

Regarding the broader market recovery, it's been two years since the 2020 low point when elective volumes dropped 40-60% across categories. Global med device procedure volumes are now up 3% from 2019 per Evaluate MedTech, with us leading at 6%. Facilitators include fixed supply chain issues—stent lead times down to two weeks from eight—and hospital capital expenditure returning to normal, with U.S. centers planning over $10 billion for robotics in 2024. Challenges linger, like 7% labor cost hikes squeezing margins and 5% inflation in raw materials such as titanium and polymers. Yet, enduring factors—an anticipated 20% rise in the global 65+ population by 2030 and climbing chronic conditions, with AFib up 25% per ESC stats—support mid-teens long-term growth.

To capitalize, we're advancing key efforts: ramping robotic uptake with VeriFlex's AI haptic feedback reaching 85% OR penetration in new sites, trimming procedure times 22% and lifting consumables attach to 95%; launching Procedure Analytics for EHR-integrated predictive scheduling, showing 10% efficiency gains in pilots; and progressing the pipeline, with FDA nod expected soon for EvoCore Ultra TAVR in Q4 2023 featuring a 15% smaller profile preferred by two-thirds of heart teams, plus the $450 million NeuroDyn acquisition enhancing neuromodulation with next-gen DRG capabilities.

For the outlook, we expect Q4 procedure volumes at 13-15% year-over-year, with full-year at the upper end of our prior 12-14% band. Potential risks encompass U.S. recession impacts on electives or European reimbursement pressures, but our 65% recurring revenue and share gains offer resilience.

Now, let's talk about competitive dynamics and market share trends.

The third quarter represented continued market share expansion across our core franchises, fueled by our unique offerings and sharp execution amid evolving competition. Drawing from our internal metrics and validated by sources like Millennium Research Group and Evaluate MedTech, here's the breakdown.

Broadly, the global structural heart market—45% of our revenue—expanded 12% year-over-year to about $12.5 billion, propelled by deeper TAVR and mitral tech penetration. We lifted our share from 7.2% last year to 9.1% this quarter, the third straight sequential gain. This beat the market through rapid uptake of EvoFlow TAVR, now 28% of our structural heart installs versus 18% a year prior. Its 14 French delivery—slimmer than rivals' 16-18 French—captured 15% share in high-risk cases prioritizing efficiency.

In orthopedics, 30% of revenue, the joint replacement sector grew 8% to $22 billion, despite earlier resin supply hiccups. We advanced knee share from 6.8% to 7.5% via the Triad Cementless Knee System, whose porous titanium boosts osseointegration 22% over Stryker's Triathlon in preclinical tests shared at last month's AAOS. Hip share held at 5.2%, but we're progressing in ambulatory surgery centers with modular designs saving 12 minutes per OR case.

The competitive field is fragmented yet consolidating. Edwards Lifesciences leads structural heart at 18.5% share with Sapien 3 Ultra, but their 9% growth slowed as our EVOLVE trial data showed 2.3% lower paravalvular leak rates via radial access. Abbott's MitraClip owns 62% of transcatheter mitral repair, but our post-ValveX acquisition ClipFlow has grabbed 4% share, with volumes up 35% quarter-over-quarter. Medtronic's CoreValve Evolut at 14% TAVR share faced setbacks from an FDA warning on manufacturing, shifting 200 basis points our way in U.S. bids. In electrophysiology, Boston Scientific's Farapulse PFA took 11% from RF techs, yet our CE Mark-cleared FlexPulse PFA hit 8% in EMEA with 97.4% acute success in a 500-patient registry.

By region:

U.S. (62% revenue): Up 110 basis points to 8.7% share, aided by CMS tailwinds covering 95% TAVR cases and 1,200-surgeon academies enhancing KOL support, with volumes 14% ahead of 11% market.

Europe (22%): Steady at 6.9% amid NICE/HAS cost reviews, but German HTA approvals for EvoFlow—saving €2,500 lifetime vs. Edwards—boosted volumes 22%, leveraging our Dublin hub post-Brexit.

Asia-Pacific (10%): 18% market surge to $3.8 billion, but local rivals like MicroPort limited us to 4.2%; Terumo JV in Japan yielded 25% growth and 7% TAVR tender share.

Emerging Markets (6%): 20% growth, 5.1% share via low-cost ortho kits; 30% R&D for adaptations like EvoFlow Lite positions for Q1 NMPA approval.

Our strategy rests on innovation with $450 million FY24 R&D for five IDEs; clinical data like our 10,000-patient STRUCTURAL registry beating rivals on durability; and MediHub AI platform, in 40% U.S. cases for 15% outcome improvements.

Ahead, aging demographics (65+ up 3% YoY) and robotics synergies—like Intuitive bundling with da Vinci—offer tailwinds. Risks: titanium tariffs, stent erosion. We aim for 200 bps FY24 share growth, targeting top-5 status by 2026.

Moving on to key assumptions underlying the guidance.

Our full-year 2024 outlook remains at the high end: revenue $4.25 billion to $4.30 billion, or 7-9% reported and 8-10% organic growth; adjusted gross margin up 50-100 bps to 68-69%; adjusted diluted EPS $5.55-$5.65. This incorporates base cases for cardiovascular, orthopedics, and endoscopy amid macro challenges.

Core assumptions span procedures, pricing, margins, expenses, reimbursement, and macros:

Procedure growth: 6-8% globally, building on Q3's 12%. Cardiovascular: 7-9% in structural heart/TAVR, moderating U.S. from 15% IQVIA Q3 to 10% Q4. Orthopedics: 5-7% hips/knees, ASCs now 25% U.S. ortho mix vs. 18% prior.

Regions: U.S. +7% (Medicare Advantage); EMEA +4-6% (UK tenders offset German DRGs); APAC +10-12% (China NMPA for Zenith Alpha, India hospitals).

Pricing/mix: Flat to +1% ASP, +50 bps from high-acuity like AI endoscopy (15-20% premiums). U.S. GPO pressure offset by value contracts; Europe MDR renewals; EM +2-3% localization.

Gross margins: +75 bps to 68-69% via $150M Vitalis Efficiency Program—Galway automation (200 bps stents), Anoka resin to 95%. Raw inflation +3%, FX -1% (euro 1.08), no Red Sea issues (85% air).

OpEx: 48-49% revenue, 5-6% growth for leverage. R&D 12% for VSR-300 (FDA Q1 2025), bioresorbables; $200M M&A no diluters.

Reimbursement: Stable 2025 OPPS +2.5% APCs cardiovascular, no deep MPFS cuts; China NRDL $50M volume.

Macros: U.S. GDP +2.2%, healthcare +5.5%; 2% elective deferrals; 100 bps structural heart share gain; VCP 105.

Risks: Inventory destock, Euro recession (-50 bps EMEA), FDA VSR-300 delays ($100M shift). Upside: China tenders, ASC >30%.

High conviction for guide top-end, setting 10%+ 2025 organic.

Finally, organic revenue growth by segment and geography.

Excluding NeuroVasc Solutions acquisition and FX, we achieved 9.2% organic growth, up from Q2's 7.8%, exceeding 7-9% guide—strongest since Q4 2021, thanks to volumes, share in structural heart, pipeline ramps, and elective macros.

By segment (YoY organic):

CRM (28% revenue): 12.5%, 17% volumes in Azure XT/PulseGuard ICDs/pacs; BlueSync 45% attach (vs. 32%), Medicare S-ICD, Epic integration; +1% pricing, +120 bps U.S. share (Millennium).

Structural Heart/Vascular (32%): 14.8%, TAVR +22% EvoFlex launch (95% success, 10% lower price vs. Sapien); stents +9% EluNIR; peripheral Tack 15% PAD share.

Orthopaedics (22%): 6.7%, EMEA softness; Mako +25% (1.2M cases); BioBrace sports +18% ACL.

Endoscopy/Neuro (18%): 7.9%, SpyGlass DS +11% ERCP vs. Olympus; neuro flat lapping Pipeline; Intellis SCS +14% CPTs.

Geography:

U.S. (52%): 11.4%, electives +19% outpatient, CMS TAVR, DTC campaigns >9% market.

EAME (25%): 6.2%, Europe flat (NHS/French tariffs), ME double-digits (Vision 2030); endoscopy +12%.

APAC (15%): 8.9%, Japan +14% Shonin/Mako; China +4% post-VBP (-18% pricing), India/SE Asia +22%.

EM (8%): 13.6%, Brazil/Mexico reforms.

Under Procedural Excellence: 12% R&D ($250M 2024 incl. AI TAVR, Vertex hypertension); 85% derisked supply (Mexico/Vietnam); +200 bps mix.

Q4: 9-11% organic, U.S./APAC upside. Risks: China VBP, Euro inflation; 45% recurring buffers.

I will now turn the call over to Rachel for a review of our financial results.

Rachel Kim:
Thank you, Mark. As Mark outlined, we delivered a strong financial performance this quarter.

Total revenue reached $1.08 billion, up 9% as reported and 9.2% organically, aligning with the segment and geographic breakdowns Mark detailed. Recurring revenue from consumables and services hit 65% of total, providing stability.

Gross profit was $739 million, yielding an adjusted gross margin of 68.5%, up 80 basis points year-over-year from manufacturing efficiencies in our Galway and Anoka facilities, favorable product mix toward high-margin structural heart, and the Vitalis Efficiency Program savings. Raw material costs rose modestly as anticipated, offset by fixed contracts.

Operating expenses came in at $520 million, or 48.1% of revenue, with SG&A up 5% on commercial expansion and R&D at 12.3% funding pipeline milestones like VSR-300 and EvoCore Ultra. Adjusted operating margin expanded to 20.4%, driving adjusted diluted EPS of $1.42, up 12% year-over-year.

Cash flow from operations was robust at $280 million, supporting $150 million in share repurchases and debt reduction. We ended the quarter with $2.1 billion in cash and equivalents.

For full-year guidance, as Mark noted, we're holding at $4.25-4.30 billion revenue, 68-69% gross margin, and $5.55-5.65 adjusted EPS, based on the key assumptions provided.

Now, I'll turn the call back to Mark for Q&A.

Mark Ellison:
Thank you, Rachel. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from Mike Rossi with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Rossi:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Mark, on procedure volumes, you called out strong U.S. acceleration to 17%—can you expand on Q4 visibility and any signs of backlog reformation?

Mark Ellison:
Thanks, Mike. Great question. Our visibility into Q4 remains strong, with early surgeon surveys and hospital scheduling data pointing to sustained 13-15% growth. In the U.S., the 17% reflects cleared backlogs and staffing improvements, but we're not seeing reformation—in fact, OR utilization is trending toward our 90% target. Obesity tailwinds and CMS hikes keep momentum, though we'd watch recession signals closely.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jennifer Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Lee:
Hi, team. Rachel, on competitive dynamics, you mentioned share gains versus Edwards and Medtronic—how sustainable with their scale, and any pricing read-through?

Rachel Kim:
Hi Jennifer. Sustainability comes from clinical differentiation—like EVOLVE's leak data and FlexPulse's PFA success—and our training programs. Edwards slowed, Medtronic's warning helped, but we're gaining on merits. Pricing stable overall; no aggressive erosion expected, with value contracts flooring ASPs amid GPO pressure.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Baker with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Baker:
Thanks. Dr. Vasquez, on the pipeline like EvoCore Ultra and VeriFlex enhancements—walk us through technical edges and adoption timelines.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Tom. EvoCore Ultra's smaller profile and AI deployment improve access and precision, with heart team preference in trials. VeriFlex's haptic AI cuts times 22%, 85% penetration. FDA Q4 for Ultra; VeriFlex Europe ramping now. Our registries like STRUCTURAL and ADVANCE provide evidence for rapid uptake.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Kim:
Good morning. Mark, on guidance assumptions, with China VBP and Euro risks—how much cushion in the top-end revenue?

Mark Ellison:
Alex, solid point. We've built conservatism: China volumes via localization despite -18% pricing; Euro assumes DRG softness but HTA wins. U.S. anchor at 7%, upside from ASCs/China tenders could add $50-100M. High conviction for top-end given procedural strength.

Mark Ellison:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to reiterate our confidence in the long-term growth potential of Vitalis MedTech. We are committed to delivering innovative medical device solutions that improve patient outcomes and create value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
